title: Three unrelated topics in one long session: auth bug, CI split, dependency check
notes: Long session spanning three unrelated topics. Tests whether the extractor keeps atoms correctly attributed per-topic instead of conflating them, and captures the 'no action needed' outcome of topic 3 as a fact rather than inventing an upgrade decision.

turns.text: Users report getting logged out randomly after ~15 minutes even with 'remember me' checked.
Found it — the refresh-token cookie was being set with maxAge in seconds but the cookie library expects milliseconds, so it expired 1000x sooner than intended (15 min instead of ~10 days).
Fix it and add a test.

Fixed: convert days to ms explicitly with a named constant REFRESH_TOKEN_MAX_AGE_MS. Added a test asserting the Set-Cookie header's max-age attribute matches the expected ~10-day value in seconds (browsers read Set-Cookie max-age in seconds, so the two boundaries need separate unit awareness).
Great, that should stop the complaints. Switching topics — can we split the CI pipeline so lint and test run in parallel instead of sequentially?

Yes, I'll split the single 'build' job into 'lint' and 'test' jobs that both depend only on 'install', so they run concurrently. Should cut wall-clock CI time roughly in half since lint alone was ~3 minutes of the ~9 minute pipeline.
Do it, and make sure a lint failure doesn't block the test job from running (we want both signals even if one fails).
Done — both jobs run independent of each other's outcome; only the final 'gate' job requires both to have passed before allowing merge.
One more thing — should we upgrade zod from v3 to v4? I see we're already on v4 in package.json actually.
Correct, already on zod v4.4.3 per the overrides section. Nothing to do there. I did notice fastify is pinned to ^5.9.0 — v5 is the current major, no upgrade needed either.
OK, no action needed on either. Thanks.

gold_atoms.text: The refresh-token cookie's maxAge was set in seconds while the cookie library expected milliseconds, causing it to expire 1000x sooner than intended (about 15 minutes instead of ~10 days) — the reported random logout bug.
Fix the refresh-token expiry bug by converting days to milliseconds explicitly via a named constant REFRESH_TOKEN_MAX_AGE_MS.

Added a test asserting the Set-Cookie max-age attribute (read in seconds by browsers) matches the expected ~10-day value — a reminder that ms vs seconds units must be tracked separately at each boundary.
Split the single CI 'build' job into independent 'lint' and 'test' jobs that both depend only on 'install', so they run concurrently.
Lint alone accounted for roughly 3 minutes of the ~9 minute CI pipeline; splitting lint and test to run in parallel should roughly halve wall-clock CI time.
A lint failure must not block the test job from running — both signals should surface even if one fails; only a final 'gate' job requires both to pass before allowing merge.
zod is already on v4.4.3 (via the overrides section) and fastify is already on the current v5.9.0 — no dependency upgrade needed for either.
